source_note: Compiled from official notices and mainstream reporting. Every card links to its original source.

items.title: UK universities withdraw student offers amid stricter visa rules
items.summary: Some UK universities are reported to be withdrawing admission offers previously made to Indian students. The withdrawals are linked to stricter visa rules and rising refusal rates affecting international applicants from India and other countries.

items.title: US green card policy costs examined for India's IT industry
items.summary: An analysis examines the impact of current US green card policies on India's information technology sector. The report explores what these immigration rules cost the Indian IT industry in terms of talent and business.

items.title: US ends 540-day automatic work permit extension for immigrants
items.summary: The United States has ended the 540-day automatic extension of work permits for certain immigrants. The change affects how long work authorization remains valid while renewal applications are pending with immigration authorities.

items.title: US visa and green card applicants face new filing deadline rules from Oct 23
items.summary: New filing deadline rules for US visa and green card applicants take effect from 23 October. The changes affect how and when applicants must submit their immigration paperwork to US authorities.

items.title: New USCIS deadline rules: What green card and H-1B applicants must know
items.summary: US Citizenship and Immigration Services has introduced new deadline rules affecting green card and H-1B visa applicants. The changes tighten timelines for filing and responding to immigration requests and notices.

items.title: New USCIS rules tighten deadlines for Green Card and H-1B applicants
items.summary: United States Citizenship and Immigration Services has introduced new rules that tighten deadlines for Green Card applicants and H-1B workers. The changes affect filing requirements and timelines for these visa categories, though specific details of the modifications have not been disclosed in this report.

items.title: UK universities withdraw admission offers as visa refusals rise for Indian students
items.summary: Universities in the United Kingdom are reportedly withdrawing admission offers to Indian students as visa refusal rates increase. The trend appears linked to tighter student visa rules being implemented, affecting students who had already received university acceptance letters for study programmes.

items.title: US visa rule change: Weekend timing could affect Green Card applicant eligibility
items.summary: A change to United States visa rules means that weekend timing could impact eligibility for some Green Card applicants. The modification to how deadlines are calculated may cause some applicants to lose their eligibility depending on whether key dates fall on weekdays or weekends.

items.title: UAE's five-year multiple-entry tourist visa rules for Indian travellers
items.summary: The UAE offers a five-year multiple-entry tourist visa option for Indian travellers. The report explains the rules, requirements and conditions that Indian passport holders need to know when applying for this long-term tourist visa.

items.title: UK student visa applications fall 16% as August total drops below 100,000
items.summary: Student visa applications to the UK declined by 16 per cent, with the August total falling below 100,000. The drop reflects changing patterns in international student applications to British universities and colleges.

items.title: Switzerland visas for Indians: New mobility pact vs young professionals scheme
items.summary: A new mobility pact between India and Switzerland is compared with the existing young professionals scheme. The report explains how the two visa pathways differ for Indians seeking to work or study in Switzerland.

items.title: PERM ban affects green card path beyond H-1B workers
items.summary: A reported ban on PERM labour certification affects not only H-1B visa holders but also other categories of workers seeking permanent residency in the United States. The change impacts the green card pathway for multiple visa categories that rely on employer sponsorship through the PERM process.

items.title: Indian students in Australia face challenges with rent, jobs and visa concerns
items.summary: Indian students studying in Australia are encountering difficulties navigating high rental costs, employment challenges and visa-related worries. The report suggests that the experience on the ground is proving harder than the initial promise that attracted students to choose Australia for their education.

items.title: UK universities withdraw admission offers to Indian students as visa refusals rise
items.summary: Some UK universities are reported to be withdrawing admission offers to students from India, Pakistan and Nigeria. The withdrawals are linked to rising visa refusal rates affecting applicants from these countries.

items.title: Dubai family visa salary requirements for bringing spouse, children or parents
items.summary: The article outlines the minimum salary requirements for Indians working in Dubai who wish to sponsor family members on a UAE family visa, including spouses, children or parents.

items.title: New Zealand employer work visa reset: Detail less dramatic than it sounds
items.summary: New Zealand First has announced changes to employer work visa rules that initially sound significant. However, the actual detail of the policy reset is reported to be less revolutionary than the announcement suggests.

items.title: Infosys says green card suspension will have no material impact on operations
items.summary: Infosys has stated that the reported suspension of green card processing will not materially affect its business. The article explains what Indian employees and applicants should understand about the current situation.

items.title: Canada PR for Indians: Who benefits from the new immigration rules?
items.summary: Canada has introduced new immigration rules affecting permanent residency applications. The article examines which categories of Indian applicants are likely to benefit from the updated policy framework.

items.title: US probes nine universities over J-1 exchange visas amid tighter student rules
items.summary: The US administration is reportedly investigating nine universities regarding their J-1 exchange visa programmes. The probe comes as part of tightened regulations affecting international students under the current administration.

items.title: Green card freeze: Impact on Indian IT companies and alternative options
items.summary: The reported green card freeze is expected to affect certain Indian IT companies and their employees more than others. The article discusses which firms face the greatest impact and explores alternative visa or relocation options.

items.title: UK student visa crackdown leaves international applicants caught between parties
items.summary: International student visa applicants to the UK are reportedly caught in difficulties between universities and the Home Office due to an ongoing visa crackdown. The situation is creating uncertainty for prospective students.

items.title: US tightens visa and green card rules for Indian tech workers
items.summary: The United States has reportedly tightened visa and green card regulations, prompting Indian technology professionals to consider alternative destinations for overseas employment and permanent residency. The article suggests five other countries as potential options for Indian tech workers.

items.title: US green card move reported to affect thousands of IT workers
items.summary: A recent US green card policy change is reported to impact thousands of IT workers. The move has been described in terms suggesting significant consequences for workers in the technology sector seeking permanent residency in the United States.

items.title: Student visa applications drop as UK tightens visa and work rules
items.summary: Student visa applications to the UK have declined following stricter visa and work regulations. The tightening of rules appears to be affecting the number of students applying to study in the United Kingdom.

items.title: US green card suspension: implications for Indian IT workers on H-1B visas
items.summary: The suspension of certain US green card processes has specific implications for Indian IT workers currently holding H-1B visas. The development affects the permanent residency pathway for this group of workers in America.

items.title: US expands crackdown on green cards and student exchange visas
items.summary: The United States has widened its enforcement actions affecting both green card applications and student exchange visas. The expanded crackdown represents a broader tightening of immigration policies across multiple visa categories in the country.

items.title: Canada PR pathway for Indians: who benefits from new immigration rules?
items.summary: New immigration rules in Canada have created a permanent residency pathway with specific benefits for certain groups of Indian applicants. The changes define which categories of applicants stand to gain from the updated regulations.

items.title: H-1B alternatives: can L-1 and O-1 visas open another US route for Indians?
items.summary: L-1 and O-1 visas are being examined as potential alternative pathways to the United States for Indian workers. These visa categories may offer different routes for those seeking to work in America beyond the H-1B programme.

items.title: US green card freeze: how PERM works and why Indian techies are affected
items.summary: A freeze on US green card processing through the PERM system is impacting Indian technology workers. The article explains the PERM labour certification process and the reasons why Indian tech professionals are particularly affected by this suspension.

items.title: US green card delays: options for Indian tech workers if PERM is suspended
items.summary: With PERM suspension causing green card delays, Indian technology workers in the US have alternative options to consider. The article outlines possible pathways available to affected workers facing interruptions in their permanent residency applications.

items.title: US green card delays: What options do Indian tech workers have if PERM is suspended
items.summary: With the suspension of the PERM labour certification process in the United States, Indian technology workers face delays in their green card applications. The article explores alternative options available to affected Indian tech professionals seeking permanent residency in America.

items.title: UK student visa applications fell sharply in September
items.summary: Student visa applications to the United Kingdom experienced a significant decline in September. The sharp drop in applications follows recent policy changes and may reflect reduced interest from international students, including those from India, in studying in Britain.

items.title: Coalition plans 650,000 cut in temporary migrants over four years
items.summary: Australia's Coalition has announced plans to reduce temporary migration by 650,000 people over a four-year period. This proposed policy change could significantly impact temporary visa holders and those planning to migrate to Australia on temporary visas.

items.title: US suspends Indian IT firms Cognizant, TCS, Wipro, HCL from Green Card filings
items.summary: The United States has suspended major Indian IT companies including Cognizant, TCS, Wipro and HCL from filing Green Card applications. The suspension affects employees of these firms seeking permanent residency through their employers in the US.

items.title: Canada asylum rules change November 3: What unfinished IRCC Portal claims must do
items.summary: Canada is changing asylum rules effective November 3. Those with unfinished claims on the IRCC Portal need to take specific action before the rule change takes effect to ensure their applications are processed properly.

items.title: Indian students face tougher New Zealand visa rules as approval rate falls to 49.3%
items.summary: New Zealand has introduced tougher visa rules for Indian students, with the approval rate dropping to just 49.3 per cent. This represents a significant decline in visa success rates for Indian applicants seeking to study in New Zealand.

items.title: New Zealand student visa approvals for Indians fall to 49.3% in 2026
items.summary: Official data from Immigration New Zealand shows that student visa approval rates for Indian applicants have fallen to 49.3 per cent in 2026. The figures indicate a significant tightening in visa approvals for Indian students seeking to study in New Zealand.

items.title: New Zealand changes parent resident visa rules with new 90:10 EOI system
items.summary: New Zealand has changed its parent resident visa rules, introducing a new 90:10 Expression of Interest system. Indian applicants seeking to bring their parents to New Zealand will need to understand the updated requirements under the revised EOI framework.

items.title: UK student visa refusals rise: What tougher rules mean for Indian students
items.summary: Student visa refusals from the United Kingdom are on the rise, with tougher rules now affecting Indian students. The stricter regulations are making it more difficult for Indian applicants to secure approval for study visas to the UK.

items.title: Planning UK January 2027 intake? Key deadlines and what students need to do now
items.summary: Students planning to apply for the United Kingdom's January 2027 intake need to be aware of upcoming key deadlines. The article outlines what prospective students should be doing now to prepare their applications for the winter intake.

items.title: UK student visa refusals rise: What tougher rules mean for Indian students
items.summary: Student visa refusals for the UK have increased, indicating tougher rules are being applied. Indian students applying for UK study visas are facing stricter scrutiny and higher rejection rates under the new enforcement measures.

items.title: New Zealand student visa approvals for Indians fall to 49.3% in 2026
items.summary: Immigration New Zealand data shows student visa approval rates for Indian applicants have fallen to just 49.3 percent in 2026. This represents a significant decline in approval rates for Indian students seeking to study in New Zealand.

items.title: H-1B visa violators could face $250,000 fine, 10-year ban under new US bill
items.summary: A new bill proposed in the United States would impose penalties of up to $250,000 in fines and a 10-year ban on H-1B visa violators. The legislation aims to strengthen enforcement against those who breach H-1B visa conditions.

items.title: New Zealand changes parent visa selection: How the new rules work
items.summary: New Zealand has changed the selection process for parent resident visas. The new rules alter how applications are processed and selected, affecting those seeking to bring their parents to New Zealand on resident visas.

items.title: Australia announces new visa rules and skilled visa priorities for 2026
items.summary: Australia has introduced migration changes for 2026 including new visa rules and updated priorities for skilled visa applicants. The changes affect how skilled workers, including Indians, will be assessed and selected under Australia's migration programme.

items.title: USCIS tightens adjustment of status process for US green cards
items.summary: US Citizenship and Immigration Services has tightened the adjustment of status process for green card applicants, leading to challenges. The stricter rules affect how applicants can transition from temporary visas to permanent residency within the United States.

items.title: US green card rules challenged as USCIS tightens adjustment of status
items.summary: The US Citizenship and Immigration Services has tightened the adjustment of status process for green card applicants. The stricter rules are facing challenges as the agency makes it harder for applicants to adjust their immigration status within the country.

items.title: When Indian visitors can change US nonimmigrant status without leaving
items.summary: US immigration rules allow certain Indian visitors to change their nonimmigrant status while remaining in America without having to leave the country. The regulations specify conditions under which status changes can be applied for from within the United States.

items.title: Australia tightens student visa rules on English, visa hopping and dependants
items.summary: Australia has tightened student visa rules for Indian students with changes to English language requirements at level EL3, restrictions on visa hopping between courses, and new limitations on bringing family members as dependants on student visas.

items.title: Canada updates and personalises work permit processing times
items.summary: Canada has updated its work permit processing time system with personalised estimates for applicants. The changes affect how Indians can check expected processing times for their specific work permit applications based on individual circumstances and application type.

items.title: Australia limits dependants for international students
items.summary: Australia has tightened student visa rules and introduced new limits on dependants for international students. The changes restrict the ability of students to bring family members with them or sponsor dependants while studying in Australia.

items.title: Canada Express Entry explained: How the PR system works for Indians
items.summary: An explanation of how Canada's Express Entry permanent residence system operates and what Indian applicants should understand before applying. The report covers the key aspects of the PR pathway and important considerations for prospective applicants from India.

items.title: New Zealand changes Parent Resident Visa selection process from today
items.summary: New Zealand has changed the selection process for its Parent Resident Visa category, with the new system taking effect immediately. The changes alter how applications are selected and processed for parents seeking to join their children in New Zealand as permanent residents.

items.title: US EB-2 visa cutoff for India remains at November 2013
items.summary: The October 2026 US Visa Bulletin shows the EB-2 employment-based green card cutoff date for India remains stuck at November 2013. This means Indian applicants who filed after that date continue to face lengthy waits for permanent residency.

items.title: US demands up to $20,000 visa bond from 50 countries; India excluded
items.summary: The United States is requiring visa bonds of up to twenty thousand dollars from applicants in fifty countries. Indian passport holders have been left out of this bond requirement and are not affected by the new measure.

items.title: What Indians need to know about Canada visa biometrics before applying
items.summary: Indians applying for Canadian visitor, student, work or permanent residence status must provide biometrics as part of their application. The report outlines what applicants need to know about the biometric requirements before submitting their visa applications to Canada.

items.title: Australia's new student visa measures now in effect for Indian applicants
items.summary: Australia has implemented new student visa measures that are now in effect. Indian applicants need to understand the changed rules when applying for student visas to Australia. The new measures introduce specific requirements that affect how Indian students can apply.

items.title: Four big Green Card changes to take place before 2027 impacting Indians
items.summary: Four significant changes to the US Green Card system are expected to take place before 2027 that will impact Indian applicants. The changes will affect how Indians navigate the permanent residency process and their timelines for obtaining green cards.

items.title: 28-day rule can derail UK student visa applications despite sufficient funds
items.summary: Indian students applying for UK student visas must comply with a specific 28-day rule regarding their financial documentation. Even if applicants have enough money to meet visa requirements, failing to follow this timing rule can result in visa application rejection.

items.title: What F-1 student visa applicants should know about social media vetting
items.summary: US visa officers now check social media accounts of F-1 student visa applicants. Indian students applying for US student visas should be aware that their social media presence will be reviewed as part of the application process and vetting procedures.
